questions: Did line_loss_events fall below 1 on the s-bend and slalom with the 12 mm footprint on the iteration 2 body and track?
Did max_error change from the iteration 2 values (0.061 to 0.069)? If not, the footprint is not the limit.
Did steering_oscillation rise or fall with the smaller footprint, which gives sharper sensor contrast?
On the oval, which dips to progress 0.11, does the robot leave the tape in the first bend or after a long straight? Does the progress value suggest a start-up transient?

intent: Isolate the sensor footprint effect by returning the body and drivetrain to the iteration 2 values and changing only sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m. Expected result: max_error stays near 0.06 or improves slightly, and line_loss_events is 0 or 1. If line loss clears and max_error drops below 0.06, the footprint was the limit and I will keep 0.012 m. If nothing moves, the next change is wheel_radius to 0.035 m to test speed.
learning: If the footprint change does nothing, the geometry levers that remain untested are wheel_radius (speed) and the sensor lead at the far edge of the 0.08 m forward limit. Those are the next candidates. I will judge every geometry change by whether max_error stays under the fixed 0.06 m limit and whether line_loss_events falls to 0.
rationale: Iteration 3 scored 46.71, below iteration 1 (50.13) and iteration 2 (50.07). Narrowing the track to 0.10 m, shortening the body to 0.12 m and reducing mass to 0.5 kg did not reduce line loss. Every track still shows one line-loss event and max_error of 0.061 to 0.067, which is at the 0.06 m off-track limit. The s-bend rms error fell (0.026 to 0.022), but its progress also fell (0.15 to 0.13), so the lighter, narrower body did not help the robot reach the next bend. Across four iterations, sensor span, footprint, lead and drivetrain changes have each left max_error almost unchanged. Turning authority is therefore not the main limit. The score is cut short by a drift that starts early and reaches the 0.06 m limit, while the robot is still well short of the finish (progress 0.10 to 0.15). Two things are still untested in isolation: the 12 mm footprint with the widened array (iteration 0 used 12 mm but a narrower span), and wheel_radius, which affects the speed the robot reaches before the drift grows. I revert the drivetrain and body to the iteration 2 values (mass 0.6, body_length 0.18, wheel_track 0.12) because iteration 2 gave the better s-bend progress. I keep the iteration 2 sensor layout (x = -0.03 to 0.03 m, y = 0.04 m) and change only sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m. This isolates the footprint effect, which the Integrator asked for. I expect little change in max_error (the array is not the binding limit), so a failure to move would confirm that the limit lies elsewhere, most likely speed or the controller's response to the motor mismatch. If max_error falls below 0.06 with line_loss 0, the footprint was the cause and I will move to wheel_radius next.
